content: This can easily be adapted to knowledge graphs by constructing paths of entities and relations. In particular, a random walk on a knowledge graph starting at entity $e_{1}$ and ending at entity $e_{k}$ is a sequence of the form $e_{1}, r_{1}, e_{2}, r_{2}, \cdots ,e_{k}$ representing the entities and the corresponding relations between $e_{1}$ and $e_{k}$ in the knowledge graph. Moving forward we denote such a path of entities and relations by $\mathbf {q}=(e_{1},r_{1}, e_{2}, r_{2}, \cdots ,e_{k})$ . We generate a large set of such paths from the knowledge graph G by performing several random walks on it which in turn yields a corpus of “sentences” S needed for “language modeling”.
